summary: Iter16 is a non-destructive backend check of identifier uniqueness in UNIV-2026-BO-01. 8/8 pytest tests pass. (1) In the DB, the 1040 ánforas have numero_anfora values exactly 1..1040 with no duplicates. The 520 mesas have no duplicate numero_mesa. Recinto names have no duplicates after trim/casefold. The 3 partial unique indexes uniq_anfora/mesa/recinto_UNIV_2026_BO_01 exist (unique=true, partialFilterExpression={id_eleccion: UNIV-2026-BO-01}). (2) Every linked acta matches: numero_anfora equals its ánfora's number and ambiente equals 'Mesa {numero_mesa}', with 0 mismatches. (3) As admin, these PUTs returned 409: ánfora with another ánfora's number padded with spaces, mesa with another mesa's number, and recinto with another recinto's name in UPPERCASE. The documents are byte-identical afterwards. (4) The equivalent POSTs returned 409 and inserted nothing: ánfora with a duplicate number, mesa with a duplicate number, and recinto with a duplicate name in lowercase with spaces. (5) Snapshot hashes of anforas_mesa, mesas_sufragio, recintos_electorales and actas (eleccion) are identical before and after the run. Global actas total is 1042, with 855 esta_bloqueada=true (same as iter15). The public /resultados endpoint still reports ánforas 1040/852/188. The normalization endpoint was NOT invoked.
critical_code_review_comments: _validar_unico_en_eleccion loads every document of the election (to_list(50000)) on each POST/PUT and compares in Python. This is O(n) per write. Consider storing a normalized field (e.g. numero_anfora_norm) with a unique index.

The check-then-insert is not atomic. For UNIV-2026-BO-01 the partial unique index only blocks exact-value races, not case or whitespace variants. Other elections have no DB-level protection, so two concurrent requests can both pass the check. Catch DuplicateKeyError -> 409, and consider creating indexes for every election.

PUT ánfora/mesa/recinto does not propagate changes to the linked actas (numero_anfora, ambiente, recinto). Only the normalization endpoint does. Renaming through the PUT endpoints will desync the actas.
PUT recinto/mesa runs the uniqueness check before checking that the document exists. A missing id with a duplicate value returns 409 instead of 404 (minor ordering issue).
The stored values are not trimmed: 'X ' is saved as-is (e.g. acta.recinto 'Fac. Ciencia y Tecnología ' has a trailing space). Normalize on write.
The normalization endpoint uses update_many without a transaction. A partial failure would leave a mixed state. It should not be re-run casually.
The login field is 'contrasena', not 'password'. Note this for future tests.
